title: Gated compute provisioning interface (IMP-0015 slice 2): budget-gated, write-ahead reserved, budget-derived auto-stop, fake provider only
summary: provision.py exposes provision/status/stop/destroy/reconcile, each returning the persisted job record (JSON-able dict). Records live at <orchestrator_home()>/compute-jobs/<job_id>.json and are written atomically with storage.write_json. A job moves through a persisted lifecycle state machine: requested -> reserved -> launching -> running -> stopping -> stopped -> destroyed -> reconciled. blocked is reachable only from requested and is left only by a new provision() call, which re-evaluates it (blocked -> requested, reason retry, in history) against the current budget. That keeps the default idempotency key usable after an operator approves or raises the budget. failed is reachable from requested through stopped (launching -> failed only once instance_id is known), and failed -> destroyed|reconciled. Any unlisted transition raises ValueError. Precondition: budget.effective(request.budget, budget_home) is approved, both caps are set, and estimate.high <= job_hard_cap_usd and <= project_usd. Otherwise the job is blocked with a reason, and nothing is reserved or launched. Write-ahead, as in IMP-0013/DEC-0020: the job persists requested, appends a ledger reservation of estimate.high, persists reserved, then persists launching before provider.launch. Ledger appends are idempotent per (job_id, kind), and a found reservation means the gate already passed. Validation requires estimate.high > 0. Mandatory auto-stop: max_runtime_seconds = floor(min(requested runtime, estimate.high / hourly_usd * 3600)), computed during the precondition check before the ledger reservation is written (a value <= 0 is requested -> blocked, so reserved -> blocked is never needed), so billed runtime never exceeds the budget cap. The provider enforces it (survives Agent OS dying) and status() enforces it as well, which is why compute.status is annotated readOnlyHint: false, destructiveHint: false. Reconcile appends actual (defaulting to the polled provider cost) and a release whose amount is this job_id's 'reserved' ledger entry (from the idempotency scan, not record.reservation_usd, so a crash between the ledger append and persisting reserved leaves no orphan reservation), then records variance against the expected estimate. Idempotency key: an explicit job_id, else cj-<sha256(canonical request)[:12]>. provider.launch is idempotent launch-or-lookup by spec name = job_id, so resuming a crashed launching step is safe. If launch raises, the job stays launching with the reservation held, because the provider may have created the instance. A later provision resumes onto the same instance. destroy abandons the launch: it calls launch-or-lookup to learn the instance_id, then goes launching -> failed, terminates, and goes to destroyed, and only then can reconcile release the reservation. destroy on a requested or reserved job (no instance_id, nothing launched) goes to failed (reason abandoned) and then destroyed without any provider call, and reconcile then releases the ledger reserved amount, so a reservation never needs a launch to be freed. No instance is left untracked while its reservation is released. Secrets are accepted only as a secrets:// reference, stored and never resolved in this slice. Raw credential keys or values raise ValueError before anything is persisted. compute_fake.py defines the provider protocol (launch/poll/stop/terminate) and an in-memory FakeProvider with an injectable clock and no network. Any non-fake provider name is blocked: a real launch still needs a write-enabled key and operator confirmation (slice 3). Exposure: `orchestrate compute provision|status|stop|destroy|reconcile` and MCP tools compute.provision/status/stop/destroy/reconcile. The full contract is pinned in docs/model-infrastructure.md, section 'Gated provisioning interface (slice 2)'.

prior_art.checked: agent-os orchestrate prior-art lookup "cloud GPU brokers (SkyPilot); cluster lifecycle autostop" -> PA-skypilot (BORROW), PA-dstack (DEFER), PA-runpod-python (BORROW), PA-temporal (REJECT)
prior_art.found: SkyPilot: a cluster status set (INIT/UP/STOPPED, then terminated by down), the cluster name as the launch idempotency key (sky launch -c <name> reuses an existing cluster), and autostop/--down enforced on the cluster side. dstack: an equivalent lifecycle, but with its own server. runpod-python: pod create/get/delete payloads, already mirrored by the stdlib client in foreman_deploy.py. Temporal: durable execution with a server cluster.
prior_art.reused: SkyPilot status set mapped onto launching/running/stopped/destroyed; SkyPilot name-as-idempotency-key for provider.launch; SkyPilot provider-side autostop idea, made budget-derived instead of idle-derived; IMP-0013/DEC-0020 write-ahead intent pattern; budget.effective and the budget.record_spend reserved/actual/release ledger (DEC-0041); storage.write_json for atomic records
prior_art.why_custom: SkyPilot is too heavy to embed in the stdlib runtime (DEC-0009), has no spend reservation or operator budget gate, and its autostop is idle-based. The registry already records that an in-house RunPod lifecycle supersedes the spike-first step, so the interface is provider-neutral and in-house, and SkyPilot remains a WRAP candidate behind the same protocol if a second GPU cloud is needed. Temporal is rejected (server cluster); file-based write-ahead is enough at this scale.
